name: elephant
about: Chain ragdoll body for the elephant (31-bone quadruped rig, identical skeleton to the wolf's). 13 capsules: hips (root, spine0), chest, head (neck + head + jaw: the trunk is skinned to the head and jaw bones, so it hangs off and swings with the head capsule; there is no separate trunk body), tail_a, tail_b, and 4 legs x (upper, lower). Bones without a body (spine1, spine3, spine4, ears, pasterns, paws, tail1, tail3) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. Heavy, thick torso and column legs with narrow swing. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured. The torso radius is capped by the 31-bone rig: the legs sit only 0.0789 model units off the spine, so torso + leg radii must stay under that or the start pose overlaps (test/chain-quadrupeds.test.mjs checks it).
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json original-elephant scale.model 5: bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale (about 4.7 m long, 2.5 m at the ear tip)
mass_assumption: placeholder: a real African elephant is about 3 m at the shoulder and 4 to 6 tonnes; this one is 2.5 m at the ear tip and 4.7 m long, call it 2.6 tonnes. The game data gives hp 150 and no mass.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: own: the creature faces +z. A hind hock flexes the lower leg backward (-z); a front elbow flexes it forward (+z). Same convention as the salamander.

segments.source: placeholder: spine2 to neck (spine3, spine4 ride on it); stiff spine
placeholder: neck to jaw (neck + head + jaw; the trunk and tusks ride on it, the ears too)
placeholder: tail2 to tail3 plus 0.05 model units past the last bone
placeholder: low, pastern and paw as one capsule; rests at about 36 degrees, folds less than a wolf's
